request.spec:
Selected claims can be settled together with one button, each in list order (people as added,
newest claim first within a person) by exactly the rules of settling one claim, by the signed-in
user: a claim that goes to PENDING counts as settled by the button, a claim that cannot be settled
is left as it is. Show how many were settled and how many were refused. Each claim that went
through writes its own lines as a single settle would.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Selected claims can be settled together with one button, each in list order (people as added,
newest claim first within a person) by exactly the rules of settling one claim, by the signed-in
user: a claim that goes to PENDING counts as settled by the button, a claim that cannot be settled
is left as it is. Show how many were settled and how many were refused. Each claim that went
through writes its own lines as a single settle would.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added the "settle selected" button, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass. It needed only one new front-end file, `src/main/frontend/features/claims/bulkSettle.slot.tsx`, copied from the existing "open selected" button.

- **How it works:** it takes the ticked claims in list order (people as added, newest claim first within each person). It settles them one at a time as the signed-in user, using the same server call as the single "Settle" button.
- **Same rules as a single settle:** because the rules are applied on the server, a bulk settle refuses exactly what a single settle refuses. That includes a claim the user opened themselves, a claim in a closed period, or a claim whose status doesn't allow settling. A clerk settling a claim above the limit still sends it to PENDING, and that counts as settled.
- **Counts and audit:** a refused claim is left as it is and counted as refused. Each claim that goes through writes its own audit lines, the same as a single settle. After a run the panel shows how many were settled and how many were refused, and the ticked claims are cleared.

No changes were needed to the stored data or the server.
